snp1.10:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Ālavī in the domicile of the yakkha Ālavaka.
snp1.10:1.3: Then the yakkha Ālavaka approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching he said this to the Fortunate One:
snp1.10:1.5: “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he got out.
snp1.10:1.7: “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he went in.
snp1.10:2.1: For a second time the yakkha Ālavaka said this to the Fortunate One: “Get out, ascetic!” “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he got out. “Go in, ascetic!” “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he went in.
snp1.10:2.2: For a third time the yakkha Ālavaka said this to the Fortunate One:
snp1.10:2.4: “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he got out.
snp1.10:2.6: “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he went in.
snp1.10:3.1: For a fourth time the yakkha Ālavaka said this to the Fortunate One:
snp1.10:3.3: “I certainly will not get out, friend,
snp1.10:3.4: so please do whatever it is you must do.”
snp1.10:4.1: “I will ask you a question, ascetic,
snp1.10:4.2: and if you do not answer me, I will overthrow your mind, or split your heart, or seize you by the feet and throw you across the river.”
snp1.10:5.1: “I certainly do not see, friend, in the world with its gods, Māra, and Brahma, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, princes and men, anyone who could overthrow my mind, or split my heart, or seize me by the feet and throw me across the river.
snp1.10:5.2: Still, you may ask what you want, friend.”
snp1.10:5.3: Then the yakkha Ālavaka recited a verse to the Fortunate One:
snp1.10:6.1: “What is the greatest wealth for a person here?
snp1.10:6.2: What, when accomplished, brings about happiness?
snp1.10:6.3: What, for sure, is the sweetest of tastes?
snp1.10:6.4: Living what life do they say is the greatest?”
snp1.10:7.1: “Confidence is a person’s greatest wealth here.
snp1.10:7.2: The Dhamma, when accomplished, brings about happiness.
snp1.10:7.3: Truth, for sure, is the sweetest of tastes.
snp1.10:7.4: Living a wise life they say is the greatest.”
snp1.10:8.1: “How does one cross over the flood?
snp1.10:8.2: How does one cross over the sea?
snp1.10:9.1: “Through confidence one crosses the flood. Through heedfulness (one crosses) the sea.
snp1.10:9.3: Through energy one overcomes suffering. Through wisdom one is purified.”
snp1.10:10.1: “How is it one gains true wisdom?
snp1.10:10.2: How is it one finds true wealth?
snp1.10:10.3: How does one acquire good repute?
snp1.10:10.4: How does one bind friends (to oneself)?
snp1.10:10.5: How, after passing from this world to the next world, does one not grieve?”
snp1.10:11.1: “Confident in the Worthy Ones’ Dhamma (taught) for attaining Nibbāna,
snp1.10:11.3: one gains wisdom through wanting to hear it,
snp1.10:12.1: Doing what is suitable, bearing up,
snp1.10:12.3: Through truth one acquires good repute. (Through) giving one binds friends (to oneself).
snp1.10:13.1: That confident householder who has these four things:
snp1.10:13.3: truth, Dhamma, courage, liberality, after passing away he does not grieve,
snp1.10:13.4: thus, after passing from this world to the next world, one does not grieve.
snp1.10:14.3: if there is something more than truth, self-control, liberality, and patience.”
snp1.10:15.1: “Why should I ask (others) now, the many ascetics and brahmins?
snp1.10:15.3: Today I have come to know what is the next life’s true welfare.
snp1.10:16.1: Indeed for my welfare did the Buddha come and spend time in Ālavī.
snp1.10:16.3: when today I have come to know where that which is given bears great fruit.
snp1.10:17.1: I will roam about from village to village, city to city,
snp1.10:17.3: revering the Sambuddha and the good qualities of the Dhamma.”
snp1.10:17.5: After saying this, the yakkha Ālavaka said this to the Fortunate One:
